newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway's central bank cuts key interest rates.
newsitem.headline: Norway's central bank cuts key interest rates.

text.p: Norway's central bank announced on Wednesday it was cutting its key interest rates, effective from Thursday.
The bank said it was trimming its overnight deposit rate, to 3.5 percent from 4.0 percent. The overnight lending rate was reduced to 5.5 percent from 6.0 percent.
The cut was expected and the money market had discounted for a 50 basis point cut.
Central Bank governor Kjell Storvik said the decision came in response to developments in the money and foreign exchange markets.

"The crown exchange rate has recently been under persistent pressure, and since the reduction in interest rates on November 5, 1996, Norges Bank (central bank) has purchases foreign currency equivalents to NOK 38 billion, of which a good NOK 15 billion has been purchased since the beginning of 1997," the bank said in a statement.
The bank said the crown had appreciated to the strongest level against Europan currencies since it was floated in December 1992.

The crown has been firming for months because the economy is strong and foreign investors have been buying Norwegian currency due to short term money market rates which have been markedly higher than their German equivalent.

The primary objective of Norwegian monetary policy is exchange rate stability, but the central bank has been worried about cutting rates because this could drive up inflation and overheat the oil-rich country's booming economy.
The bank said there were clear limits on it's scope for manoeuvre in the operational application of monetary policy.
"Against this background and in view of the extensive interventions that have been carried out, a reduction in interest rates is necessary to stabilise the exchange rate," it said.
However the crown, which stood at 100.64 on the inverse ECU index at 1430 gmt, half an hour before the cut, firmed slightly following the announcement.
The three-month eurokrone swap rate, which stood at 3.66 percent at 1430 gmt, was down 10 basis points half an hour after the announcement.
